title: Audit log instrumentation: Dedicated capacity scaling + quota/admin changes (before/after + auto/manual source)
creator: Nadia Rahman
description:
Context
Dedicated capacity scaling and quota/admin changes are explicitly in-scope “sensitive actions” for the audit logging program. Today, Dedicated has partial logs (and some are non-normalized / missing before/after values), which is blocking enterprise questionnaires and internal coverage gating.

Scope
Instrument audit events for Dedicated capacity + quota/admin actions across:
1) Manual admin actions via Console / internal admin tooling
2) Automated changes initiated by autoscaler / controllers

Must include:
- before + after values for each change
- source of change: auto vs manual (and sub-source when available)
- request_id / trace_id correlation (when invoked via API/Console)
- actor attribution that clearly distinguishes human user vs service identity

In-scope actions (initial set)
A) Capacity scaling
- Change desired capacity (GPU count or “replica”/pool size depending on Dedicated backend)
- Update autoscaling policy (min/max, target utilization, cooldowns)
- Enable/disable burst capacity (if applicable)

B) Quota + admin changes
- Update customer/org quota for Dedicated (e.g., max GPUs, max concurrent requests, max tokens/sec, max RPM)
- Change account state impacting availability (pause/resume, disable routing, block traffic)

Out of scope
- Routine autoscaler decisions that do not change configured state (e.g., internal scheduling) unless they modify desired capacity / min/max / quota
- Non-sensitive observability events

Event naming (proposed)
Follow audit event naming guidelines with a dedicated namespace.
- dedicated.capacity.desired.updated
- dedicated.capacity.autoscaling_policy.updated
- dedicated.capacity.burst.updated
- dedicated.quota.updated
- dedicated.account_state.updated

Schema requirements (must pass schema v1 validator)
- event_version: “1.0”
- event_name: from registry
- occurred_at: RFC3339
- org_id, workspace_id (if applicable), dedicated_pool_id (or equivalent)
- actor: user|service with stable IDs
- target: resource identifiers (dedicated_pool / quota_config)
- request: request_id + trace_id when available
- source:
  - change_source: “manual” | “auto”
  - source_system: “console” | “api” | “autoscaler” | “control-plane” | “support-tooling” (best-effort)
- outcome:
  - status: “success” | “failure”
  - error_code + error_message (sanitized) on failure
- diff/before_after payload:
  - before: relevant fields
  - after: relevant fields
  - fields_changed: list of field names (to support quick filtering)

Before/after payload guidance
- Always include only the fields relevant to the action. Avoid dumping full objects if they may contain secrets or unbounded metadata.
- Examples:
  - desired_capacity before/after
  - autoscaling.min_replicas / max_replicas / target_utilization before/after
  - quota.tokens_per_second / quota.max_concurrent_requests before/after
  - account_state before/after (e.g., “active” -> “paused”)

Implementation notes
- Primary emit point should be the control-plane service that persists the change (source of truth), not the UI.
- If UI triggers change, pass request_id/trace_id and actor through to the control-plane.
- For auto changes: actor.type=service, actor.name in {“dedicated-autoscaler”, “dedicated-controller”}. change_source=auto and source_system=autoscaler/controller.
- For manual changes: actor.type=user (or “service” for support tooling with impersonation). If impersonation exists, include both “actor” (the tool/service) and “on_behalf_of” in the audit event per schema guidance.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] All in-scope Dedicated capacity scaling and quota/admin change paths emit schema-v1 compliant audit events.
- [x] Events include before/after and fields_changed.
- [x] Events include change_source=manual|auto and source_system.
- [x] Events are registered in the audit event registry; build-time check passes.
- [x] Unit tests cover event payload construction + redaction guardrails.
- [x] Integration test (staging) performs at least one manual and one auto scaling/quota path and asserts event presence + required fields.
- [x] Coverage scanner reflects these sensitive actions as covered for Dedicated subsystem.

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - desired capacity update -> asserts before/after + manual source
  - autoscaler update path -> asserts change_source=auto + service actor
  - quota update -> asserts before/after, fields_changed
- Staging integration:
  - Console: change desired capacity for a test pool; verify event in audit log pipeline with matching request_id
  - Autoscaler: trigger policy evaluation leading to desired capacity change; verify event with actor=dedicated-autoscaler

Rollout
- Ship behind feature flag AUDIT_DEDICATED_SCALING_V1 initially enabled in staging.
- Production: enable for 10% orgs (enterprise beta) then ramp to 100% once SRE confirms no delivery lag regression.

References
- Linear initiative: PM-411
- Related work:
  - Shared library/validator: ENG-2482
  - Coverage scanner: ENG-2491
- GitHub PR (implementation): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18533
- Customer escalation context: SUP-4977 (missing Dedicated admin actions in audit logs)
comments: 2025-05-29 (Nadia Rahman): Creating ticket as part of audit logging sensitive-actions inventory. Dedicated scaling/quota changes are a top enterprise requirement; we’ve had at least one support escalation about missing admin actions.

2025-06-03 (Rafael Mendes): Confirmed current behavior: manual capacity changes are persisted in control-plane but only emit an internal log line (no schema-v1 audit event). Autoscaler changes desired capacity without any audit event today. Plan is to emit in control-plane write path and attach actor/request context where available.

2025-06-05 (Miles Thornton): For reliability/SLO analysis we need fields_changed and consistent pool identifiers; please include dedicated_pool_id and region where known (region can be part of target metadata). Also ensure we don’t emit excessive event volume; only emit on persisted config changes.

2025-06-07 (Marcus Lin): +1 to emitting at source of truth. For auto changes, actor must be a service identity (no blank actor). On failure outcomes, sanitize error_message (no internal stack traces) and do not include auth tokens/headers.

2025-06-10 (Rafael Mendes): Open question: quota updates sometimes occur via support-tooling service with user impersonation. Proposal: actor=service(support-tool), on_behalf_of=user_id. Will align with schema v1 guidance and keep user attribution for auditors.

2025-06-14 (Rafael Mendes): PR up with new events dedicated.capacity.desired.updated and dedicated.quota.updated including before/after + fields_changed. Autoscaler path emits dedicated.capacity.desired.updated with change_source=auto and actor=dedicated-autoscaler. Added unit tests and wired request_id propagation when invoked via Console.
2025-06-18 (Chloe Martin): Confirmed Console path now passes request_id/trace_id to control-plane for capacity updates; audit events in staging show correct correlation. Pagination/export unaffected.

2025-06-21 (Nadia Rahman): Marking Done. PR 18533 merged; coverage scanner shows Dedicated scaling/quota actions covered. Follow-up: ensure docs/inventory mapping reflects final event names and add integration test coverage in ENG-2492 if not already included.
